Create a complete single self-contained file `chip8_openrouter-moonshotai-kimi-k3_01.html` (HTML + CSS + JavaScript inline;
no external libraries, CDNs, assets or backend). Build a working CHIP-8 emulator.

Implement the interpreter properly: 4 KB of memory with the font set loaded at 0x050 and programs at 0x200,
sixteen 8-bit registers V0 to VF, the 16-bit index register, the program counter, a call stack, and the
delay and sound timers counting down at 60 Hz. Decode and execute the complete instruction set of 35
instructions, including the arithmetic and logic group with the carry and borrow flags in VF, the shift
instructions, jumps and calls, the random instruction, BCD conversion, register save and load, and the key
tests.

The display is 64 by 32 pixels drawn on a canvas scaled to a readable size, with sprites drawn by XOR and
the collision flag set in VF. The 16-key keypad is mapped to a 4 by 4 block of keyboard keys shown in the
interface; key press and release must both reach the emulator.

Include a small demo ROM as a byte array inside the file: a real program, assembled by you, that draws a
sprite and moves or reacts to a key, so that the emulator can be tried without any download. Also allow
loading a ROM from a local file.

Add run, pause, single step and reset controls, an adjustable instructions-per-frame speed, and a debugger
panel showing the registers, the index register, the program counter, the stack and the decoded current
instruction. Every visible control must work. Deliver the one file `chip8_openrouter-moonshotai-kimi-k3_01.html`.

I'll create this CHIP-8 emulator as a single self-contained HTML file. Since it's a large file, I'll use the full-file generation tool with a precise spec — including a hand-assembled demo ROM I've already worked out (sprite at 0x230, main loop polling keys 4/6/2/8 to move an 8×5 alien sprite with screen wrapping).

- Main layout: left column = screen + controls + keypad; right column = debugger panel.

  Row1: 1 2 3 C
  Row2: 4 5 6 D
  Row3: 7 8 9 E
  Row4: A 0 B F
  Each cell shows the CHIP-8 hex digit large and the mapped keyboard key small. Keyboard mapping: 1->1, 2->2, 3->3, 4->C, q->4, w->5, e->6, r->D, a->7, s->8, d->9, f->E, z->A, x->0, c->B, v->F. Cells highlight (CSS class) while the corresponding key is physically held.

  - I register (4 hex digits), PC (4 hex digits), SP (2 hex digits).
  - Delay timer and Sound timer values.

- reset(): clear memory/display/registers/stack/timers, reload fontset, pc=0x200, then reload the currently loaded ROM bytes (keep a copy of last loaded ROM).
- loadRom(bytes, name): reset machine, copy bytes to memory at 0x200, store name.
- cycle(): fetch opcode = memory[pc]<<8 | memory[pc+1]; pc += 2; decode and execute. Implement the COMPLETE classic 35-instruction set with these exact semantics (x = (op>>8)&0xF, y = (op>>4)&0xF, n = op&0xF, nn = op&0xFF, nnn = op&0xFFF):
  - 0NNN: call RCA 1802 program — implement as no-op.
  - 00E0: clear display, drawFlag=true.
  - 00EE: return: pc = stack.pop().
  - 1NNN: pc = nnn.
  - 2NNN: stack.push(pc); pc = nnn.
  - 3XNN: if V[x]===nn pc+=2.
  - 4XNN: if V[x]!==nn pc+=2.
  - 5XY0: if V[x]===V[y] pc+=2.
  - 6XNN: V[x]=nn.
  - 7XNN: V[x]=(V[x]+nn)&0xFF (no carry flag).
  - 8XY0: V[x]=V[y].
  - 8XY1: V[x]|=V[y].  8XY2: V[x]&=V[y].  8XY3: V[x]^=V[y].
  - 8XY4: sum=V[x]+V[y]; V[0xF]=sum>255?1:0; V[x]=sum&0xFF.
  - 8XY5: V[0xF]=V[x]>=V[y]?1:0; V[x]=(V[x]-V[y])&0xFF.
  - 8XY6 (COSMAC VIP behavior): V[0xF]=V[y]&1; V[x]=V[y]>>1.
  - 8XY7: V[0xF]=V[y]>=V[x]?1:0; V[x]=(V[y]-V[x])&0xFF.
  - 8XYE: V[0xF]=(V[y]>>7)&1; V[x]=(V[y]<<1)&0xFF.
  - 9XY0: if V[x]!==V[y] pc+=2.
  - ANNN: I=nnn.
  - BNNN: pc=nnn+V[0].
  - CXNN: V[x]=Math.floor(Math.random()*256)&nn.
  - DXYN: draw 8-wide, n-row sprite at (V[x],V[y]) from memory I..I+n-1; XOR each pixel onto display (64x32, clip pixels outside screen — do not wrap); V[0xF]=1 if any set pixel was unset (collision), else 0; drawFlag=true.
  - EX9E: if keys[V[x]]===1 pc+=2.
  - EXA1: if keys[V[x]]===0 pc+=2.
  - FX07: V[x]=delayTimer.
  - FX0A: blocking key wait: implement with a waitingForKey register index; while waiting, pc does NOT advance (re-execute same opcode each cycle); when any key k is pressed, V[x]=k and clear waiting state. Implement by: if not waiting, set waiting=x and pc-=2 (so opcode refetches); each cycle while waiting, scan keys, on first pressed key set V[x]=k, clear waiting, pc+=2.
  - FX15: delayTimer=V[x].  FX18: soundTimer=V[x].
  - FX1E: I=(I+V[x])&0xFFFF.
  - FX29: I=0x050 + V[x]*5.
  - FX33: BCD: memory[I]=Math.floor(V[x]/100); memory[I+1]=Math.floor(V[x]/10)%10; memory[I+2]=V[x]%10.
  - FX55: store V0..Vx into memory at I..I+x; I unchanged (modern behavior).
  - FX65: load V0..Vx from memory at I..I+x; I unchanged.
  - Unknown opcode: console.warn.
- Main loop with requestAnimationFrame (~60 fps): each frame, if running, execute `instructionsPerFrame` cycles (from slider); then decrement delayTimer and soundTimer once per frame if >0 (this gives 60 Hz); if drawFlag, render canvas: fill black, then fillRect(1x1) in #33ff66 for each set display pixel (canvas is 64x32, CSS scales it); update debugger panel DOM every frame.

Function disassemble(op) returning mnemonic strings for the debugger, e.g.: "CLS", "RET", "JP 0x234", "CALL 0x234", "SE V3, 0xAB", "SNE V3, 0xAB", "SE V3, V4", "LD V3, 0xAB", "ADD V3, 0xAB", "LD V3, V4", "OR V3, V4", "AND V3, V4", "XOR V3, V4", "ADD V3, V4", "SUB V3, V4", "SHR V3, V4", "SUBN V3, V4", "SHL V3, V4", "SNE V3, V4", "LD I, 0x234", "JP V0, 0x234", "RND V3, 0xAB", "DRW V3, V4, 5", "SKP V3", "SKNP V3", "LD V3, DT", "LD V3, K", "LD DT, V3", "LD ST, V3", "ADD I, V3", "LD F, V3", "LD B, V3", "LD [I], V3", "LD V3, [I]", "SYS 0x234", "DB 0x??" for unknown.

=== DEMO ROM (embed EXACTLY these 53 bytes as a Uint8Array; auto-load on page load so it runs immediately) ===
[0x60,0x08, 0x61,0x08, 0x73,0x01, 0xA2,0x30, 0xD0,0x15,
 0xD0,0x15, 0x62,0x04, 0xE2,0xA1, 0x80,0x35, 0x62,0x06, 0xE2,0xA1, 0x80,0x14,

This program: V0=x=8, V1=y=8, V3=step=1, I=0x230 (sprite), draws an 8x5 alien sprite, then loops: erase sprite (XOR redraw), poll key 4 (left: V0-=1), key 6 (right: V0+=1), key 2 (up: V1-=1), key 8 (down: V1+=1), wrap x with AND 0x3F and y with AND 0x1F, redraw, jump back to loop start at 0x20A. Sprite rows: 3C 7E DB FF 66. - Pause: running=false.
- Step: if running, pause first; execute exactly one cycle; force one render + debugger update.
- Reset: reset machine, reload current ROM, keep paused state (running=false), render cleared screen, update debugger.

- Keyboard: keydown/keyup listeners; map keys (lowercase, also handle event.code-independent via key.toLowerCase()); set keys[k]=1/0; toggle highlight class on the keypad cell; preventDefault for mapped keys so page doesn't scroll/trigger.
